question_text: What is the Characteristic Impedance (Z_0) of a lossless transmission line, and how is it calculated from its lumped-element model?
answer_text: Z_0 = sqrt(L / C) (where L is inductance per unit length, and C is capacitance per unit length).
explanation_text: Characteristic impedance is not a DC resistance you can measure with a multimeter. It's the instantaneous ratio of voltage to current (V/I) that a high-frequency wave experiences as it travels down the line. It is determined entirely by the line's parasitic inductance and capacitance.
bonus_question_text: Does the length of the transmission line affect its Characteristic Impedance?
bonus_answer_text: No. Because Z_0 is determined by the ratio of L and C *per unit length*, a 1-inch 50Ω trace and a 10-foot 50Ω cable have the exact same characteristic impedance.
